nodes.label: Raspberry Pi 4 Model B Single-Board Computer
nodes.description: Top-down photograph of a green Raspberry Pi 4 Model B PCB (silkscreen 'Raspberry Pi 4 Model B, (c) Raspberry Pi 2018', FCC ID 2ABCB-RPI4B, Made in the UK). Visible: Broadcom SoC under a metal lid, LPDDR4 SDRAM package, 40-pin GPIO header (J8), gigabit Ethernet jack, 2x USB 3.0 and 2x USB 2.0 stacks, USB-C power in, dual micro-HDMI (HDMI0/HDMI1), CSI camera connector (J3), DSI display connector (J4), 3.5mm A/V jack, PoE header (J14), RUN/GLOBAL_EN test points.
nodes.rationale: Selected as the edge controller because it combines enough CPU/RAM to run computer-vision inference locally with the GPIO, USB and camera I/O needed to drive relays and read sensors on one board, avoiding a separate microcontroller.

nodes.label: 40-Pin GPIO Header (J8)
nodes.description: Double-row 2x20 male header along the top edge, silkscreened 'GPIO' / 'J8'. Provides 3.3V/5V rails, ground, and digital I/O lines used to drive actuator control signals and to read digital sensor outputs.

nodes.label: USB Host Ports (USB 3.0 J12 / USB 2.0 J11)
nodes.description: Two stacked dual-port USB blocks on the right edge: blue-tongue USB 3.0 (J12) and black USB 2.0 (J11). These are the attachment point for a UVC webcam used as the imaging input.

nodes.label: CSI Camera Connector (J3)
nodes.description: 15-way FFC ribbon connector silkscreened 'CAMERA' / 'J3' for the native MIPI CSI-2 camera module — the alternative imaging path to a USB webcam.
nodes.rationale: Offers a lower-latency, non-USB imaging route; choosing USB webcam over CSI trades ribbon-length and driver simplicity against CSI's dedicated bandwidth.
